classification.difficultyReason: Choose among right, straight, opposite and full-turn relationships in a mixed set, reusing intermediate angles.

content.prompt: Calculate the value of the unknown angles. You do not need to show reasoning.

spec.description: Three separate arms point up-left, up-right and down-left. Upper and right sectors each carry 70°; the remaining left sector carries a°. No arcs or dots.
spec.mathematics: Three sectors around a point; a = 360 − 70 − 70. Preserve the source's schematic proportions; the two left arms are not collinear.
spec.answerVisibility: Only a°, 70° and 70° appear in the question; the supplied 220° answer is separate.

answer.worked:
Angles at a point sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}a&=360^\circ-70^\circ-70^\circ\\a&=220^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Vertical and rightward arms form a marked right angle. A diagonal divides it, with 25° beside the vertical and m° beside the horizontal. No dots.
spec.answerVisibility: The 65° supplied answer is excluded from the question.

answer.worked:
Angles in a right angle sum to $90^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}m&=90^\circ-25^\circ\\m&=65^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A narrow upward V has 35° inside. A reflex arc follows the outside from the left ray, around the bottom, to the right ray. y° lies below the vertex inside the reflex arc.
spec.mathematics: The marked unknown is the reflex angle, y = 360 − 35.
spec.answerVisibility: The 325° supplied answer is excluded from the question.

answer.worked:
Angles at a point sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=360^\circ-35^\circ\\y&=325^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two straight lines cross as a wide X. 100° is in the top sector and a° in the opposite bottom sector. No arcs or dots.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied 100° answer remains separate from the 100° given.

answer.worked: $a=100^\circ$ because vertically opposite angles are equal.

spec.description: A gently descending straight line crosses a steeper descending line. m° labels the upper-left acute sector and 44° the opposite lower-right sector. No arcs or dots.
spec.answerVisibility: Only m° and the given 44° are visible in the question.

answer.worked: $m=44^\circ$ because vertically opposite angles are equal.

spec.description: Two straight lines cross. Left sector 95°, opposite right sector a°, bottom sector b°; top sector unlabelled. No arcs or dots.
spec.mathematics: a = 95 by vertically opposite angles; b = 180 − 95.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied values a = 95° and b = 85° belong only to the answer.

answer.worked:
$a=95^\circ$ because vertically opposite angles are equal.

Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}b&=180^\circ-95^\circ\\b&=85^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Three separate arms extend left, up-right and down-right. Upper sector 140°, right sector 75°, lower sector p°. No arcs or dots.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied 145° answer is excluded from the question.

answer.worked:
Angles at a point sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}p&=360^\circ-140^\circ-75^\circ\\p&=145^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upward and rightward arms enclose a marked right angle. A rising diagonal separates 48° beside the vertical from x° beside the horizontal. No dots.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied 42° answer is excluded from the question.

answer.worked:
Angles in a right angle sum to $90^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}x&=90^\circ-48^\circ\\x&=42^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A gently descending straight line has an additional up-right arm. Above the line, 110° is between the left arm and extra arm; f° is between the extra arm and right arm. No arcs or dots.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied 70° answer is excluded from the question.

answer.worked:
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}f&=180^\circ-110^\circ\\f&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Four separate arms extend up-left, up-right, down-right and down-left. A square marks the upper sector. The left sector is 105°, right sector 82° and bottom sector t°. No dots or collinearity assumptions.
spec.mathematics: Four sectors around a point: t = 360 − 105 − 90 − 82. Coordinate directions preserve the marked right angle and do not create intersecting straight lines.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied 83° answer is excluded from the question.

answer.worked:
Angles at a point sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}t&=360^\circ-105^\circ-90^\circ-82^\circ\\t&=83^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two descending straight lines cross, one shallow and one steeper. The left acute sector is r°, right acute sector 25°, upper obtuse sector q° and lower obtuse sector p°. No arcs or dots.
spec.mathematics: r = 25 by vertically opposite angles; p = 180 − 25 = 155; q = p.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied values r = 25°, p = q = 155° are answer content only.

answer.worked:
$r=25^\circ$ because vertically opposite angles are equal.

Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}p&=180^\circ-25^\circ\\p&=155^\circ\end{align*}$$
$q=155^\circ$ because $p$ and $q$ are vertically opposite angles.

spec.description: A lower-right vertex joins leftward and upward arms with a right-angle square. Two internal up-left arms partition the right angle into three sectors, each labelled x°. No equal-angle arcs or dots.
spec.mathematics: Three equal angles fill 90°, so x = 90 ÷ 3.
spec.answerVisibility: All three x° labels are visible; the supplied 30° answer is separate.

answer.worked:
Three equal angles make a right angle.
$$\begin{align*}x&=90^\circ\div3\\x&=30^\circ\end{align*}$$
